findings.title: getSubGroupsCount() silently returns null for a deleted group, inconsistent with the adapter's contract elsewhere
findings.body: When the underlying group has been deleted concurrently, `getSubGroupsCount()` now returns null instead of throwing. Every other path in GroupAdapter that fails to load the delegate (`getDelegateForUpdate()` at line 61 and `isUpdated()` at line 74) throws `IllegalStateException("Not found in database")`, so this change introduces a third, silent behavior for the same condition. Returning a null Long is risky: GroupModel.getSubGroupsCount() is not documented to return null, and any caller that unboxes it (e.g. `== 0` comparisons) will now get an NPE at a distance from the real cause. In GroupUtils.populateSubGroupCount it results in `representation.setSubGroupCount(null)`, leaking a null count into the admin REST response rather than signaling the group is gone. Returning 0L or throwing the same IllegalStateException used by the rest of the class would keep the contract consistent.

findings.title: NPE on concurrent group deletion still possible in the paginated getSubGroupsStream overloads
findings.body: The PR fixes the NPE only in `getSubGroupsCount()`, but the sibling methods at lines 256, 262, and 268 (`getSubGroupsStream(String, Integer, Integer)`, `getSubGroupsStream(Integer, Integer)`, `getSubGroupsStream(String, Boolean, Integer, Integer)`) still call `modelSupplier.get().getSubGroupsStream(...)` with no null check. `modelSupplier` wraps `getGroupModel()`, which returns null when the group has been deleted, so the exact same concurrent-delete scenario that produced issue #40368 (a cached group being read while another thread removes it) will still produce an NPE on these paths. The fix should apply the same null handling (whatever is chosen for getSubGroupsCount) to all delegating methods that dereference `modelSupplier.get()`.

findings.title: Reader thread is never joined, so the race being tested can be missed or exceptions lost
findings.body: In `createMultiDeleteMultiReadMulti`, after `deletedAll.set(true)` the test immediately asserts `caughtExceptions` is empty, without joining the reader thread. Two consequences: (1) an HTTP request that is in flight when the flag is set can still fail after the assertion has already run, so a real regression can pass the test; (2) the thread is left running (it is not a daemon thread), leaking it and its admin-client connections for the remainder of the JVM/test-suite run. The test should signal completion, then `thread.join()` (with a timeout) before asserting. Additionally, since the thread is only started and never synchronized before deletions begin, it may not execute at all before all groups are deleted, in which case the test passes vacuously without ever exercising the concurrent read/delete path it was written to cover.
